cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Outsmart the Room
cards.instruction: Turn every clue, deduction, and secret into a contest you must solve or control first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't open the delivery email. Let me deduce where the office biscuits went. You remember how I taught you to separate clues from conclusions?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception signed for them. I'll tell everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good clue. Now let your teacher finish before you announce a solution. You've always rushed that bit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Too late. They're downstairs opening the box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell them to wait before eating. You've found a box, not identified its contents. I'll do that part first; watch how I check.

reason: Give the familiar training relationship a concrete role in the exact pursuit. Keep D137 planned-design claims distinct from D140 improvement claims, and make truth bait or procedure borrowing depend on actual B replies.
